/boston/mattress/.name: How to Get Rid of a Mattress in Boston (City Pickup Rules)
/boston/mattress/.description: How to get rid of a mattress in Boston, using the City of Boston's own rules: mattresses can't go in regular trash, how to book the City's curbside mattress pickup (6 units or fewer), what to do in buildings with 7+ units, donation options, and asking the seller to take the old one. Sources: boston.gov (checked 2026-10-21).
/boston/mattress/.caption: A 1-minute summary of this guide, with the City of Boston's rules (checked 2026-10-21). Narration is computer-generated.
transcript: How do you get rid of a mattress in Boston? Here's what the City says.
Mattresses and box springs can't go in regular trash. Massachusetts bans them from disposal.
Building with six units or fewer? Book the City's curbside pickup. It's by appointment only, online at boston dot gov, or call 311.

Put it at the curb by 6 a.m. on pickup day, or after 5 p.m. the night before. If it's soiled or has bed bugs, bag and seal it completely. Don't cut or crush it. The limit is 10 items per address per calendar year.
Seven or more units? The City won't collect it. Ask your property manager, or use a hauler from the City's list.
Donating? Some furniture banks, like Furnishing Hope and Household Goods, take clean mattresses with no stains or rips. Many donation outlets don't take mattresses at all.
Buying a new one? The City suggests asking the seller to take the old one for recycling on delivery.
Every option, with official sources, is at bye bulky dot com. Rules change, so confirm before you haul.

Sources: somervillema.gov (checked 2026-10-23).
/somerville/mattress/.caption: A 1-minute summary of this guide, with the City of Somerville's rules (checked 2026-10-23). Narration is computer-generated.
transcript: How do you get rid of a mattress in Somerville? Here's what the City says.
Since February first, 2026, Somerville charges fifty-five dollars per mattress, and fifty-five per box spring. A set counts as two items.
It's only for buildings with six or fewer units that get City trash pickup. The limit is two bulk items per property a week.
First buy a Disposal Sticker for each item. Online stickers come by mail and can take up to ten days. Once you have it, contact 311 by 3:30 p.m. the day before.
Put a sticker on each item and set it out after 4 p.m. the day before, and by 7 a.m. Nothing on top, and leave 36 inches of sidewalk clear.
Don't just put it out with the trash. Unscheduled mattresses are left on the curb and may be fined.
Seven or more units, or want to donate? Every option, with sources, is at bye bulky dot com. Rules change, so confirm before you haul.

/cambridge/mattress/.description: How to get rid of a mattress in Cambridge, MA, using the City of Cambridge's own rules: curbside collection through its contractor UTEC at $45 per mattress and $45 per box spring, booking online, curb timing (by 7 a.m., not before 6 p.m. the night before), what UTEC refuses, the Massachusetts trash ban, and no drop-off locations in Cambridge. Sources: cambridgema.gov and utecinc.org (checked 2026-10-24).

transcript: How do you get rid of a mattress in Cambridge? Here's what the City says.
Cambridge mattress pickup isn't free anymore. The City's contractor, UTEC, charges forty-five dollars per mattress and forty-five per box spring, so a set is ninety.
Book online with UTEC and choose Cambridge. The City says slots fill up quickly. UTEC takes up to eight pieces per pickup.
Put it at the curb by 7 a.m., and not before 6 p.m. the night before. You don't need to be home. The City suggests a note with UTEC, your order number and the date.
UTEC refuses torn, soiled or moldy items, anything with bed bugs or other pests, and futons, toppers, air beds and water beds.
Don't put it out with the trash. Massachusetts has banned that since 2022, and the City says there are no drop-off spots in Cambridge.
Paid haulers, donation and drop-off options, each with sources, are at bye bulky dot com. Rules change, so confirm before you haul.
